question: Enterobacteriaceae:

options.opa: They are mobile bacteria with polar flagellation.
options.opd: They do not include plant pathogens.

analysis: Enterobacteriaceae is a large family of Gram-negative bacteria that includes many well-known pathogens. They are facultative anaerobes, meaning they can use oxygen when it is available but can also switch to anaerobic respiration. One of their characteristics is the ability to reduce nitrates to nitrites, which aligns with option opb. They are typically catalase positive, which rules out option opc. They are not known for polar flagellation, as they usually have peritrichous flagella, ruling out option opa. Some members of Enterobacteriaceae can indeed be plant pathogens, which rules out option opd.
